disposition_reason: Pot experiment on six rice varieties with Cd-spiked soil and foliar Si; brown-rice Cd values are only in Fig. 3, the text gives percentage changes with and without Si, which are recorded as controls.

study.design: Pot experiment, six indica rice varieties, foliar nano-silica vs water control, n=3 pots
study.origin: Guangxi University experimental field soil, Nanning, Guangxi, China, spiked with CdCl2

controls.control: Foliar spraying of nano-silica fertilizer (1.7 g/L, twice: tillering and grain-filling) in a Cd-spiked pot soil (1.20 mg/kg total soil Cd)
controls.outcome: Brown-rice Cd increased 15.7% in WY1179 and 24.1% in YHSM (Si-stimulated varieties); decreased 34.3% to 65.7% in JLY1377, MXZ2 and YLY900 (per-variety split not printed in text); decreased in YXYLS (magnitude not printed). Absolute brown-rice Cd concentrations are shown in Fig. 3 only.

controls.control: Rice variety (six indica varieties: YHSM, MXZ2 conventional; YXYLS, JLY1377, WY1179, YLY900 hybrid)
controls.comparator: other varieties under identical Cd-spiked pot conditions without Si (CK)
controls.outcome: Highest brown-rice Cd in WY1179 and YLY900; lowest in JLY1377, MXZ2, YHSM and YXYLS (values figure-only)

unresolved: Brown-rice Cd concentrations per variety and treatment are shown only in Fig. 3 (not read off the chart).
Translocation factors (Table 3) are ratios, not concentrations. Soil, root, stem, leaf, panicle and glume Cd are non-food tissues.
Pot experiment, soil spiked to 1.20 mg/kg Cd with CdCl2; results are not a market occurrence survey.
